title: Bring back the Google scripts
lede: Two scripts, about 15 minutes. A picture of every screen, and the code on this page.

slides.cap: Both scripts ran as the Google account of the person who deployed them. That account is closed, so you deploy them again as you.

notes.html: Your Sheet is called erc-content-desk and its project ends with Sheet API; the pictures show a test copy.

steps.title: What you need
items: Chrome, signed in to your TAMU Google account and no other.
Edit access to both Sheets.
About 15 minutes.

steps.title: The two Sheets
items: erc-content-desk, the desk's Sheet: team drive Education Research Center > ERC Content Desk > Content queue. Script 1 is inside it.
subscribe to listserve, the sign-up Sheet: ERC Content Desk > Listserv. Script 2 goes inside it.
steps.links: erc-content-desk subscribe to listserve

slides.cap: Open the Sheet erc-content-desk and its script.
The editor opens in a new tab.

notes.html: A new Untitled project here is the wrong place. Stop and email the desk's owner (Who to ask).

slides.cap: Project Settings.
Further down the same page. Yours lists SHEET_API_TOKEN too: leave it. If it is missing, stop and email the desk's owner.
Adding a missing one. A folder's id is the last part of its address when the folder is open in Drive.
Back in the editor, the permissions file.
The desk script, whole.

notes.html: In the editor, paste it over the old code. Next picture.

slides.cap: The script pasted over the old code, and saved.
A small helper, run once, so Google asks for every permission the script needs.

notes.html: Click at the very end of Code.gs, after the last line, and paste. Save.

slides.cap: The end of Code.gs with the helper in place.
Run the helper.
With checkAccess picked.
Google asks before the first run.
Google's permission window opens in its own tab.

steps.title: Allow it
items: Pick your TAMU account.
If Google says it has not verified this app: Advanced, then Go to Untitled project (unsafe). Yours says the project's name.
Tick every box, or Select all.
Continue.

slides.cap: The Execution log opens under the code.
A new deployment. The old ones belong to the closed account.
The New deployment box.
The web app's settings.
The address. Keep it private: it goes to the desk's owner by email and nowhere else.
The same screens as script 1, with these differences.

steps.title: What differs
items: The Sheet is subscribe to listserve.
A new Untitled project may open. That is fine.
No settings and no properties: the Sheet's id is in the code.
The code is the second box on this page.
Run waitingCount, not checkAccess.
steps.links: subscribe to listserve

slides.cap: Open the Sheet subscribe to listserve and its script.
A project that already holds doPost and waitingCount is the old script: carry on in it. Otherwise:
The sign-up script, whole.

notes.html: In the editor, paste it over the old code. Next picture.

slides.cap: Pasted and saved, as for script 1.
Run waitingCount once. It reads Sheet 1, so Google asks for permission.
Run. The picture shows script 1's checkAccess; yours says waitingCount.
Then allow it as for script 1: your account, every box, Continue. The log ends with Execution completed.
Deploy it the same way.
A web app again.
The same settings. Who has access: Anyone, since the desk sends sign-ups without signing in.
The second address. Copy it, then Done.
The desk reaches the scripts through two settings only the owner can change.

notes.html: Email only. Never a shared doc, a chat or a page: the sign-up address alone lets anyone add rows.

steps.title: You
items: Each address in a private (Incognito) window first. The desk script reads "ERC Content Desk sheet API is running. It only accepts POST requests." and the sign-up script "The sign-up script is running." A Google sign-in page means Who has access is not Anyone.
Email both addresses to the desk's owner, at the address in READ ME FIRST - ERC Content Desk.
Say which is which: "erc-content-desk script" and "subscribe to listserve script".

steps.title: The owner, once
items: On vercel.com, team TAMU-ERC, project erc-content-desk: Settings > Environment Variables. SHEET_API_URL gets the desk script's address, LISTSERV_URL the sign-up script's. SHEET_API_TOKEN stays.
Deployments > the newest Production deployment > Redeploy. Listserv then turns from Down to Live by itself.
A later change to a script is a new version of your own deployment: the address stays, and Vercel stays as it is.

slides.cap: Once the owner says the redeploy is done, open Listserv.
One test of each script. Delete the test rows after.

steps.title: Two tests
items: On erc-share.vercel.app/listserv, sign up as "Test, delete me" with your own email. The page says "Thank you. You are on the list."
Delete that row, the last on Sheet 1 of subscribe to listserve. Listserv's Last sign-up then shows today: expected.
On Submit content, add "Test item, delete me" with the link https://example.org/test and your initials. Within a minute it is the last row on the first tab of erc-content-desk.
Delete it on Content Sort (the team password: Who to ask). Its Sheet row stays, marked trashed.

slides.cap: The scraper, the briefs and the send dates use the desk script too.

steps.title: The rest
items: Content queue > Run the scraper. Under two minutes later the line reads "Last run ..." with Open the sheet. "The last run failed on GitHub." means not yet.
Any brief on Research briefs (the team password: Who to ask) lists its files. "Drive didn't answer." means not yet.
A send date typed on the Sheet's schedule tab shows on Newsletter > Schedule within ten minutes.

slides.cap: When a check fails, the message says which side it is.

steps.title: Where to look
items: In the editor, Executions lists each call. A failed sign-up call shows as Failed: click it to read why. The desk script answers its errors in words, so its calls show Completed even when they refuse.

steps.title: A Google sign-in page in the private window
items: Who has access is not Anyone. Deploy > Manage deployments > your deployment > the pencil > Who has access: Anyone > Deploy. The address stays.
No Anyone under Who has access at all: a TAMU setting. Stop and tell the owner; an option limited to Texas A&M or to Google accounts will not work, because the desk never signs in.

steps.title: "Unauthorized: missing or incorrect token."
items: The token property changed. Do not guess a value. Email the owner.

slides.cap: Three more messages.

steps.title: "Server is not configured: the ... script property is not set."
items: Add it as in script 1's Script Properties. For SHEET_API_TOKEN, email the owner.

steps.title: "The Sheet's script does not know this action yet." or "Unknown action"
items: Old code is live. Paste the desk script from this page again, save, then a new version: next picture.

steps.title: The private window works but the desk still fails
items: The Vercel step is missing or not redeployed. In the desk's log, "Sheet API returned HTTP 403" means the desk still calls an old address.

slides.cap: Saving changes nothing live: the web app runs the code as it was deployed. To send a change to the same address, Deploy > Manage deployments, then:
A red line in the Execution log when checkAccess runs.
The traps, one line each.

steps.title: Google asked for no permission
items: Permission is asked only when a function that needs it runs. Run checkAccess or waitingCount, never doGet or doPost.

steps.title: A permission error naming Drive or Sheets
items: Google's granular consent: an empty box is a partial grant. Remove the script's access at myaccount.google.com/u/N/permissions, run checkAccess again and tick every box.
The account number in Google's addresses: N above is the number in the editor's address, such as script.google.com/u/1/. A window signed in to TAMU only has none of this.

steps.title: A change does nothing, or the address changed
items: A new deployment gets a new address; a new version keeps it. This once a new deployment was needed. Every later change is a new version of your own deployment.
Several deployments, all looking alike: pick the one with your description.

slides.cap: The rest of the traps.

steps.title: The editor opens the wrong project, or as the wrong account
items: The wrong project: always open a script from its Sheet, Extensions > Apps Script, and check the name at the top.
Several accounts in one browser: use a window signed in to TAMU only.

steps.title: Other
items: Two old helpers, checkDrive and restoreMorningScrape: the paste removes them, which is fine. Never run restoreMorningScrape.
The test address: Test deployments ends in /dev, for editors only. The desk needs /exec.
The scripts now run as you. If your account closes, whoever follows does these steps again.

slides.cap: Add a source, the Content queue's form, is in the desk script already. It needs one more script property; until then the form says "The sources sheet is not connected yet."

steps.title: Connect the sources Sheet
items: Open the Sheet Scraper sources (team drive: Education Research Center > ERC Content Desk > Newsletter). Its id is the part of its address between /d/ and /edit.
In the desk's script: Project Settings > Edit script properties > Add script property: SOURCES_SHEET_ID and that id. Save script properties. No new version needed.

steps.title: Any later change to the code
items: Replace Code.gs with the box on this page, save, and paste the checkAccess helper at the end again. Run it, and tick every box if Google asks.
Deploy > Manage deployments > your deployment > the pencil > Version: New version > Deploy. Same address. Vercel needs nothing.
